source_message.text:
You’re hired, Nikhil—congratulations. This was a strong first set: you were the only clipper to finish before the deadline, and the quality supported that result. Your moment capturing was on point, and the font selection worked well.

Two small changes should guide your work going forward. One clip was too short, so remember that clips must remain within 20-120 seconds to deliver the complete message or goal. Also, the captions and letters did not use color; adding it will make them stand out more and should improve watch time.

These are not major problems, only points of polish. Overall, your first set was strong enough to secure the position.

Payment for these clips will arrive on Thursday. After that, you’ll be properly onboarded through a better guideline video explaining exactly how we create clips, the do’s and don’ts, and what is expected.

There is also a larger responsibility ahead: you will serve as the lead clipper for a pod of 12 clippers while continuing to produce your own clips. In addition, you’ll approve work from the other 11, keep the pod operating smoothly, and make sure everyone meets the standard. Before the role begins, I’ll walk you through how all of that will work.

Congratulations again—we’ll talk soon.

source_message.text:
Hey,

I'll start with the big picture: only 6 clippers have been hired right now, and you're one of them. You're joining from the very beginning, which gives you a real opportunity to grow with this from day one.

Tomorrow, I'll send everything you need: the full training material, the guidelines, and your assigned Instagram account.

Here are the details you asked about, starting with compensation and output:

**Payment, approval, and monthly target:**
For producing 140 approved clips, the retainer is $700-900 per month. The target works out to roughly 4-5 clips per day, and maintaining consistent daily output is what will keep you on track. I personally review and approve every clip, and a clip counts toward the 140 only after I approve it. You can also earn performance bonuses based on how the clips perform on Instagram, with as much as $800 available for a single clip that blows up. That puts your earning potential well above the flat fee.

**Source videos and deliverables:**
You'll work with Arden Vale's long-form YouTube videos. Your job is to watch them, identify complete moments—a full lesson, a story, or a real point—and shape each one into a standalone 70-85 second clip for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.

That's the full setup. Get ready, and let's crush this.

Darius

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey team,

Now that the Upwork hold has been resolved, we’re moving at full speed again. First, I’m sorry about the recent delay; while we were paused, we couldn’t move as quickly as we wanted.

I used that time to develop a new system that should make your work easier and help you reach 140 approved clips faster.

The changes are:

1\. Clip variations - create a new version by keeping the same body clip and changing only the hook/opening. With this approach, you can reuse one clip up to 2-3 times. That means more clips with less work.

2\. Shorter clip styles - because these styles are faster to create and easier to combine, getting to 140 approved clips should be much smoother. If they want, some of you could even push beyond 320.

3\. Hook training video - I’m currently making a video that will show you how to identify strong hooks. One long video can provide close to 50 clip ideas. The training should make finding content both faster and easier.

Even with the delays on our side, we’ve noticed and appreciated the work, loyalty, and commitment all of you have shown. This system is meant to help you earn more without adding extra headaches.

As we expand and add more people to the team, our goal is to develop you into Lead Clippers. Progressing into those roles starts with mastering this new approach.

More examples and details are still coming. Let’s get back to work.

\- Darius

ambiguity.description: The client introduces shorter clip styles but does not clarify whether the existing 70-to-85-second range still applies to those styles.
